question: Why do cars have treaded tyres?

options.text: To increase friction and grip on the road

solution:
The correct answer is __To increase friction and grip on the road__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Treaded tyres__ are designed to increase friction between the tyres and the road surface.
 
• Treads improve the grip of tyres, especially on wet or uneven surfaces, reducing the chances of skidding.
 
• The grooves in the tread channel water away from the tyre, improving traction during rainy conditions.
 
• Better grip ensures enhanced handling and braking performance, contributing to road safety.
 
• Different tread patterns are designed for various driving conditions, such as off-road, snow, or high-speed driving.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of Tyre Maintenance:**
 
 
• Regular tyre checks ensure optimal tread depth for safe driving.
 
• Overused or bald tyres significantly reduce grip and increase stopping distances.
 
 
 
• **Types of Tyre Treads:**
 
 
• Symmetrical tread patterns are common and suitable for everyday driving conditions.
 
• Asymmetrical treads provide better cornering and wet weather performance.
 
• Directional treads are designed for high-speed performance and efficient water dispersion.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Tyre Life:**
 
 
• Driving habits, road conditions, and tyre pressure significantly influence tyre longevity.
 
• Proper alignment and rotation of tyres can help maintain even tread wear.
